newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Russia agrees to consultations with NATO.
newsitem.headline: Russia agrees to consultations with NATO.

text.p: Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov on Wednesday said Moscow had agreed to an offer from NATO to discuss issues that concerned it but reiterated Russia's opposition to expansion of the alliance.

"We were made an offer to hold consultations with NATO in order to settle any issues that might be of concern to us. We agreed to this offer. I think this will open the door to fruitful talks," Primakov told a news conference after a meeting with the 16 NATO foreign ministers.
"At the same time I would like to underline that we are sticking to our negative position towards the enlargement of NATO," Primakov said.

"This negative position is not dictated by the subjective opinions of Russia's relatively new leadership. It is an objective analysis of the fact that if NATO is enlarged.... a situation will arise which could result in new divisions in Europe."
Moscow, which has long protested that NATO enlargement would endanger its security, also wants to negotiate an agreement governing future relations with the alliance.
But although he said Russia wanted a document which would specifically deal with its concerns, Primakov gave no indication of when he thought talks on the treaty might start.
